questions.q: What are the three new marts/intermediate models this chapter built, beyond the staging models?
options: `int_orders__joined`, `int_payments__aggregated`, and `fct_orders`
Three new Power BI reports with no dbt models
`customers`, `stg_jaffle_shop__customers`, and `raw_orders`
A single giant model combining everything
questions.explain: These are the intermediate and marts models this chapter actually built, on top of the staging layer.

questions.q: Why does this lesson call the join-fanout bug (Lessons 13-15) the most valuable part of the project?
options: Because it was the longest lesson in the chapter
Because it was the only lesson with a quiz
It wasn't valuable — it was just an unfortunate detour
It's the real job of an analytics engineer on a live project — reproduce, isolate, confirm, and fix a real production issue
questions.explain: The diagnostic sequence over three lessons models real on-the-job analytics engineering work, more than any single model-building lesson alone.

questions.q: What is deliberately left out of scope in this tier?
options: A CI/CD pipeline, dbt Cloud job scheduling, and environment configuration beyond what earlier chapters already set up
Testing the new models
Connecting Power BI to the marts
The incremental materialization decision
questions.explain: This tier's job was the model layer, the incremental decision, and the diagnostic method — not the operational tooling around running it in production.

questions.q: What does `cents_to_dollars()` get applied to across this chapter's build?
options: `status`, inside the Power BI measures
It's never actually applied — it stays unused
`order_id`, inside `fct_orders`
`amount`, once, inside `stg_jaffle_shop__payments`
questions.explain: The macro was defined and applied once, in staging, back in Lesson 7 — every downstream model and report inherits dollars, not cents.

questions.q: Where does the Advanced tier of this capstone pick up?
options: By rebuilding the Beginner tier's customers mart from scratch
It doesn't connect to this tier at all
On the same fct_orders model and the same two stakeholders, extending into operational and scaling concerns this tier left alone
With a completely different company and dataset
questions.explain: The Advanced tier builds on exactly this foundation, taking it further into the territory this tier intentionally left out of scope.
